proof_review.notes: Proofs concern abstract frontier safety under stated assumptions and do not claim a particular connector or lateness policy is universally complete.

evidence: Formal claims are labeled theorem, invariant, mechanism or evidence boundary with assumptions adjacent.
Event-time watermark E=M-L is explicitly labeled an estimate/policy rather than proof that older data cannot arrive.
Source documentation is presented as implementation semantics and examples, not universal progress guarantees.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter clearly separates deductive frontier properties, operational policy, empirical distribution choice and business finality.

evidence: The Python fixture is explicitly limited to finite records, durable positions, partitions and event timestamps.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No local calculation or passing check is generalized to unseen source records, clock behavior, token continuity or future failures.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review introduces both watermark meanings and the central counterexample; exposition moves from type/scope through scalar, composite and partitioned progress to event-time policy and operations; notation supports the proofs; the executable example makes unsafe maxima visible; and ten examples plus five solved exercises test distinct reasoning skills.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. References and local execution were checked on 2026-09-02. The finite examples do not establish source-specific token comparison, commit visibility, checkpoint atomicity, partition idleness, clock quality, lateness bounds, failover continuity, privacy handling or production retention; these require source contracts, fault testing, empirical measurement and ongoing reconciliation.
